headline: TWO SILENT DEFECTS FOUND AND CLOSED, BOTH OF THE SAME SHAPE: a checked-in record claiming one thing while reality did another, with every gate green. (1) THE PUBLISHED TYPES RESOLVED FOR NOBODY. tsconfig.dts.json compiles with moduleResolution "Node", so tsc emitted 150 extensionless relative specifiers into a package declaring "type": "module"; attw reported InternalResolutionError on 7 of 14 entry points, meaning any Next.js or "type": "module" consumer on moduleResolution node16 installed this package and got broken types for all of it. Nothing here could see it: tsc typechecks src/, every test imports src/, and smoke:consumer proves each subpath IMPORTS cleanly, which it does. The emitted output was the one artifact no gate read. Fixed by scripts/add-dts-extensions.mjs and now gated by scripts/check-published-types.mjs (attw over the packed tarball, profile esm-only, run from smoke:consumer so CI covers it without a workflows edit). PR #262. (2) THE REGISTRY MISLABELLED 24 GATES. check-validator-wiring accepted firingChannel "manual" for a gate it detected as "pnpm-meta", collapsing the only distinction the field draws. Of the 24 mislabelled, SIX actually run on every PR via pretest (audit-component-integrity, check-binding-drift, check-manifest-drift, check-registry, check-source-canon, check-tenant-tokens); the other 18 are reachable only from check:fast, check:full or their own alias, which CI never invokes. check-source-canon is the costly one: registered severity warn / channel manual while exiting 1 on any violation in CI, so THE SWISS CANON IS AND WAS A HARD-FAIL CI GATE, not the dormant warning the registry described. Channel distribution corrected from 37 manual / 14 pnpm-meta to 13 / 38. Also PR #262. THREE SHIPPED RUNTIME GUARDS WERE DEAD (PR #261): icon.tsx, deprecation.ts and TenantContext.tsx read import.meta.env, which the LIBRARY build evaluates at HDS's build time, baking it to a constant in dist/. The missing-icon warning never fired, the whole deprecation channel was silent, and TenantProvider was inert for every installed consumer regardless of VITE_TENANT_SLUG. TenantProvider now takes a slug prop, which is breaking but breaks nobody, since the old behaviour never worked once installed. REVIEW CAUGHT TWO REGRESSIONS OF MINE and both are fixed in #262: the channel relabel dropped audit-gates-supportjson's probe cohort from 39 to 15 because that script used firingChannel as a cost proxy (now an explicit ID list that fails safe), and the first commit message overclaimed 24 gates as PR-gating when only 6 are. KNOWN AND DOCUMENTED, NOT FIXED: pnpm-meta detection matches a gateScript named in ANY package.json script, invoked or not, so a dead alias satisfies it; a reviewer proved it with a fixture script named totally:unused:nobody:calls:this. SCHEMA.md now says pnpm-meta means "referenced by a script", not "runs". HDS HAS NO SECRETS SCANNING ANYWHERE: gitleaks appears in no workflow and is not installed locally, so check-secrets skips silently on every commit and CI never runs it at all.
next: MERGE ORDER, all three are green and mine: #260 (status), #261 (three dead import.meta.env guards, breaking TenantProvider slug prop), #262 (registry channel honesty + published types). #262 is based on main and carries no other branch's commits; #261 is independent.

CI HAS NO SECRETS SCAN. gitleaks is referenced in no .github/workflows file and check-secrets is pre-commit only, where it skips silently when the binary is absent (it is). Needs a workflows edit, which the bot token cannot push: add a gitleaks step to ci.yml, or install the binary in the existing job and let check-secrets run. Until then the gate is a vacuous green everywhere.

CLOSE THE pnpm-meta GAMEABILITY: detection should require the referencing package.json script to be reachable from a real entry point (a husky hook, a CI step, or pretest), not merely to exist. Today a dead alias satisfies it. This is the remaining half of the registry-honesty work.
RECONCILE severity WITH REALITY: several gates say severity warn while exiting 1 in pretest and therefore blocking CI. firingChannel is now honest; severity is not.

THREE GENERATED ARTIFACTS ARE STALE AND NOTHING REGENERATES THEM: docs/audits/TIER_AUDIT.md says 65 componentSpecs (generated 2026-06-18, real count 139) and its own header reads "audit walked 0 source files"; docs/security/sbom.json is from 2026-05-06; docs/audits/exceptions-audit.md reports 53 eslint-disable and 120 sentinels against a real 98 and 44. resolvedThisSession: PUBLISHED TYPES FIXED (#262). 150 extensionless specifiers rewritten by scripts/add-dts-extensions.mjs; every entry point now green under node16 (from ESM) and bundler. Gated by scripts/check-published-types.mjs from smoke:consumer. Canary proven both directions: rebuilding dist/types without the fixer restores all 150 and the gate exits 1 with the diagnosis; running the fixer returns it to 0. attw profile is esm-only because there is no CJS build here and node10 cannot read exports, so both of those findings are design rather than regressions; the four CSS subpaths are excluded because a stylesheet has no types to resolve.

REGISTRY CHANNEL HONESTY (#262). The manual/pnpm-meta allowance removed from check-validator-wiring; 24 entries relabelled by the validator's own detection rather than by hand. Canary proven: setting check-source-canon back to manual makes the validator exit 1 naming the drift and fails exactly the three substantive assertions in the new test while the vacuity guard still passes.

THREE DEAD SHIPPED GUARDS (#261). icon.tsx, deprecation.ts, TenantContext.tsx no longer read import.meta.env. Verified in dist/: zero import.meta.env, zero typeof process, the bare process.env.NODE_ENV member expression present. A first attempt guarded that read with typeof process, which a bundler leaves as a runtime check that a browser bundle always fails, inverting the answer in a production build; measured with esbuild and corrected before merge.

audit-gates-supportjson PROBE COHORT RESTORED (#262). It selected its cohort with firingChannel !== 'pnpm-meta', so the relabel dropped it from 39 to 15. Now an explicit ID list seeded to match main, failing safe: a gate added tomorrow is included by default.

#236 CLOSED and figma/snapshot.json is on main (PR #258). Proven along the way that no agent can ever take it: the carrier runs fine through use_figma and returns a valid checksum (90bf34df), but use_figma truncates its response at 20 KB while the file is 255 KB — 12.8x — and --ingest checksums the exact bytes. A transport ceiling, not a credential problem. Two earlier failures were misread as transcription error before the runtime was shown to return function source verbatim and all ten functions to transmit byte-perfect; the guard was never at fault. The full DoD, the --json report and where each drift item is tracked are recorded in a closing comment on #236
